entries.test: The published problems and response transcripts, together with student performance or educational difficulty assessments, would establish successes on harder problems and failures on easier ones.

entries.test: Published transcripts would show whether several cases contained correct calculation setups and correct tool answers followed by GPT-4 misinterpreting or rejecting those answers.
entries.note: Misunderstanding and refusal refer to observable responses, not inaccessible mental states.

entries.test: Public evaluations of contemporary GPT-4 with each plug-in would show error frequencies on translation-intensive problems, including spatial reasoning and sequences of disparate events.

entries.test: Public comparative evaluations would show whether contemporary LLMs had reproducible limitations in reasoning or acting on their outputs on tasks trained humans could perform.
entries.note: The universal human-capability comparison has a plain test through demonstrated capability gaps.
“Can be seen as” offers a possible interpretation of hallucinations, rather than asserting that tool integration causes them.

entries.test: The authors’ publicly documented evaluations and examples available by publication would show whether tool-assisted math and fact-checking repeatedly produced errors.
entries.note: Consistently unreliable means recurring failures, not that every answer was wrong.
